scores.label: A
scores.note: Every option rewrites the paragraph instead of the selected sentence. Each one adds Gutenberg, literacy or affordability and drops the 'some historians' hedge. Option 1 adds Gutenberg and literacy and says the press 'revolutionized' society. Option 2 adds Gutenberg and affordability and says it 'contributed substantially'. Option 3 claims a 'historical consensus' and a 'central role'. Option 4 adds Gutenberg and says the press 'fundamentally altered' history. Option 5 adds Gutenberg, says the impact was 'profound' and drops the attribution.

scores.label: B
scores.note: Every option changes 'some historians' into historians in general or a frequent view, which raises the certainty. Option 1 says 'often cited'. Option 2 gets 'attribute' backwards and generalizes to all historians. Option 3 says 'recognized by historians' and calls the press a key factor, which implies consensus. Option 4 says 'Historians view' and generalizes. Option 5 says 'frequently noted'. The options are also near copies of each other.

scores.label: C
scores.note: Option 4 drops 'some' ('Scholars have noted'), which turns a hedged view into an established fact. Other options keep the hedge but overstate 'helped cause': 'instrumental', 'crucial role', 'pivotal factor' and 'major catalyst'. Option 2 is a stiff passive.

scores.label: D
scores.note: Option 3 drops 'some' ('Historians argue'). Option 4 boosts the hedge to 'Numerous scholars'. Option 5 claims a consensus ('Scholars generally agree'). All three raise the certainty. Option 2 overstates with 'pivotal role'. Option 1 is faithful and comes first.

scores.label: E
scores.note: Every option keeps the hedged attribution, so none is labelled 0. Option 2's 'instrumental in precipitating' slightly overstates the claim. Option 3 is an awkward passive. Option 5 uses the vague 'experts' and the odd phrase 'profound alterations'.
